successors.name: Southern Rhodesia
successors.text: Southern Rhodesia: 'the territory was annexed by the United Kingdom on 12 September 1923' and its first constitution came into force on 1 October 1923

successors.name: Northern Rhodesia
successors.text: Northern Rhodesia: 'On 1 April 1924, Herbert Stanley was appointed as Governor' and the administrative machinery was 'taken over by the Colonial Office'

ledger.x: October 1890: the Company's first Administrator takes up Mashonaland.
9 May 1891: the Crown proclaims a protectorate over the Company's Mashonaland, with Matabeleland following in 1894 (the gain below carries it).
October 1893: the First Matabele War begins.
January 1894: Lobengula dies and the war ends.
January 1894: Matabeleland passes under Company rule.
1899: the Order in Council gives the Company the powers over the Lozi outer realm.
1900: North-Eastern Rhodesia is recognised as British territory under the Company.
1899-1900: the Orders-in-Council make the Company's lands north of the Zambezi British territory.
12 September 1923: the Crown annexes Southern Rhodesia.
12 September 1923: Southern Rhodesia leaves the Company.
1 April 1924: the Company's rule in Northern Rhodesia ends.
1 April 1924: Northern Rhodesia passes to the Colonial Office.

wars.name: First Matabele War
wars.outcome: British victory: the Ndebele kingdom of Mthwakazi dissolved, Matabeleland brought under BSAC control; Lobengula died in January 1894.

wars.name: Second Matabele War
wars.outcome: Page gives the campaigns' names ('Rhodesia (1896) and Mashonaland (1897)') and no result; Company rule over both continues until 1923.

wars.name: Jameson Raid
wars.outcome: The Company 'unsuccessfully attempted to stage a coup in the neighbouring Transvaal Republic'; no border changed.

certainty.note: No page opened gives the Company's boundary lines.
